segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning,
a vehicle must:
While being driven in the right turn lane,
not travel through an intersection.

elements.justification: st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}' — 'a single right lane to be used only for turning' is a turn lane of side right; rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') anchors it to the lane the subject is in (bound with s3), so the configuration is the subject's own lane and not any turn lane of the scene. Same words, same atoms as NRS_484B_223_4a. 'A single right lane' is one lane, st.lane being 'a longitudinal strip of roadway for one line of vehicles', of which st.turn_lane is a refinement: the words describe the lane the highway provides, a lane designated only for turning on the right. 'Highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095, not an aggregate) is the way the lane lies on; the lane kind alone decides the configuration.

'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (DEF-NRS-484A-320: 'every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway'); ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. Not a stand-in for a named class: the words name none. Same mapping as 'a vehicle must:' in NRS_484B_223_4a.

'Being driven in the right turn lane' is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) the right turn lane L of s1; the intersection the duty concerns is the one L leads into: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end — the carrier is an approach to that intersection' (a turn lane refines st.lane, a carrier the relation admits); st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'. Not a stand-in for the lane a lane leads into (st.lane_connectivity) or a device's governance: the relation is the source's entry topology. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's motion (agency reading).

'Travel through an intersection' is a passage through X, from the subject's entry into X (its footprint comes to overlap X, rel.occupies) to its exit, that is not a turn: drv.motion.right_turn_through_region (proposed this iteration) 'has made a turn to the right through region r, recognized as it leaves r'; its not-denoted cases ('a passage through r whose heading change is above minus turn_min, such as one straight through or a turn to the left; a heading change of minus u_turn_min or less') are exactly the travel through that the turn-only lane forbids. The duty is therefore that, at the exit of a passage entered from the right turn lane, the concept holds.

applicability: At an observation at which the subject's footprint does not overlap an intersection X and overlapped it at the previous observation (its exit from X), where at some observation from its latest entry into X (the observation at which its footprint came to overlap X, having not overlapped it at the observation before) up to that exit, the subject's footprint overlapped a turn lane L of side right (st.turn_lane) that enters X (st.lane_enters L X): the passage was made while being driven in the right turn lane. At its entry the footprint overlaps both L and X.
obligation: At that exit, drv.motion.right_turn_through_region(subject, X) holds, with step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, turn_min p.turn_heading_min and u_turn_min p.u_turn_heading_min: the passage through X from its entry to its exit was a turn to the right. A passage straight through, a turn to the left or a reversal is travel through the intersection and violates the duty. Where the entry was not observed, an interval between observations since it exceeds the step, or a yaw rate since it is missing, the verdict is unknown.

narrowings.why: 'being driven' is read through the vehicle's motion in the lane, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Subject (ru.aggregate vehicle) occupies a st.turn_lane of side right that enters intersection X (st.lane_enters); it enters X from that lane and leaves X on the far side with its heading change since entry (from kin.yaw_rate) near zero: right_turn_through_region does not hold at the exit.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Subject enters X from the right turn lane and leaves X with a heading change since entry of about a quarter turn to the right: right_turn_through_region holds at the exit.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: Subject enters X from an ordinary st.lane (no turn lane) and passes straight through; its footprint never overlaps a right turn lane entering X.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Subject enters X from the right turn lane and leaves it; kin.yaw_rate is absent on the source, so the heading change since entry, and right_turn_through_region, are unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3
scenarios.narrative: Subject's footprint overlaps the right turn lane L only at its entry into X (it overlaps L and X there), and only X afterwards; it passes straight through and exits: the condition held for part of the passage, and right_turn_through_region does not hold at the exit.

scenarios.name: occasion_s3_outside
scenarios.narrative: Subject occupied the right turn lane L earlier but moved into the adjacent through lane before reaching X; its footprint does not overlap L at its entry or afterwards; it passes straight through X: the condition held only before the passage began.

onset.justification: The concept's act begins 'at the observation at which a's footprint came to overlap r (rel.occupies), having not overlapped it at the previous observation': the passage through the intersection begins at the entry.

occasion.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which a's footprint does not overlap r, having overlapped it at the previous observation: its exit from r.

under_way.words: the heading change of a since its entry into r, integrated from its yaw rate, while its footprint overlaps r
under_way.justification: An observation inside the passage is one since the entry at which the heading change is being integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading') while the footprint overlaps X; before the entry no integration runs.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change over the turn window at which a change of course counts as a turn rather than a lane change or a drift
param_proposals.source: lane-change heading changes of a few degrees versus junction turns of about ninety degrees in naturalistic driving data

param_proposals.name: p.u_turn_heading_min
param_proposals.convention: the smallest heading change magnitude over the turn window at which a turn counts as a reversal of direction
param_proposals.source: midpoint between a right-angle turn and a full reversal of direction

segmentation.text: Every vehicle
driven upon a divided highway
must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn,
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'. No named class stands in for it.

DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section'. st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines'; st.median_or_divider: 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'; st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on — a lane, roadway, shoulder, crosswalk, stop line, median or any other part of it' ties the divider to the highway h; rel.occupies anchors the subject on h ('on a highway' maps the same way in the index). The definition's 'constructed so as to impede the conflict' states the divider's purpose and is read through its presence. 'Driven' is read through the vehicle's motion.

Each roadway of a divided highway carries one direction of travel (st.roadway: 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate'); the right-hand roadway is the one whose designated direction the vehicle travels with. Being driven on a roadway of h (rel.occupies, st.on_way) other than the right-hand one is moving against that roadway's designated direction: drv.motion.moving_against_carrier 'Road user a moves against the designated direction of travel of carrier region r' (proposed this iteration), with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance. The concept reads st.lane_direction and kin.velocity; it is not a stand-in for heading, so a vehicle pointing either way is judged by its motion.

st.median_or_divider carries an 'opening attribute where a crossover exists': 'through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space' is the subject's footprint overlapping (rel.occupies) a divider region of h that carries the opening attribute.

A crossover is a divider region with the opening attribute ('opening attribute where a crossover exists'); an intersection is st.intersection, 'the region where two roadways meet'; rel.occupies places the subject at it. 'Established by a public authority' (DEF-NRS-484A-195) is a legal status read through the feature's presence.

applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a highway h (st.highway) on which a median_or_divider region lies (st.on_way), except where the subject's footprint overlaps a divider region lying on h that carries the opening attribute (an opening or a crossover), or an intersection lying on h.
obligation: Re-binding h as in the applicability: for every roadway r lying on h (st.on_way) that the subject's footprint overlaps, drv.motion.moving_against_carrier(subject, r) with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance does not hold: the subject is not driven on a roadway of the divided highway against its designated direction. Unknown where r carries no designated direction or the subject's velocity is unobserved.

narrowings.why: 'the right-hand roadway' is read through the designated direction of the roadway the vehicle is on: it is driven on the right-hand roadway where it does not move against that roadway's direction. A source that records no direction on a divider's roadways leaves the duty unknown.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's motion on the highway, whoever or whatever controls it.
'established by a public authority' is a legal status; the crossover or intersection present on the road is its evidence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A st.median_or_divider lies on highway h; the subject occupies the roadway r of h on the far side of the divider and its kin.velocity runs against r's st.lane_direction: moving_against_carrier holds.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies the roadway of h whose st.lane_direction its velocity follows; moving_against_carrier does not hold for any roadway it overlaps.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject drives against a roadway's direction on a highway on which no st.median_or_divider lies: no divided highway.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies a roadway of the divided highway h; st.lane_direction is absent on the source, so moving_against_carrier is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject crosses the opposing roadway's edge while its footprint overlaps an intersection lying on h: the exception for an intersection holds.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

obligation: The turn is made through an opening, a crossover or an intersection: at some observation of that same window the subject's footprint overlapped a median_or_divider region lying on h that carries the opening attribute, or an intersection lying on h. Where it overlapped none of them at any observation of the window, the turn violates the duty; where an overlap is unobserved and none is observed, unknown.

'driven' is read through the vehicle's motion on the highway, whoever or whatever controls it.
'established by a public authority' is a legal status; the crossover or intersection present on the road is its evidence.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On highway h with a st.median_or_divider without opening, the subject makes a reversal of direction (drv.motion.u_turn rises) whose path crosses the divider away from any intersection and any region with the opening attribute.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: On h the subject makes a U-turn whose path overlaps a divider region carrying the opening attribute (a crossover).

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject makes a left turn on a highway on which no st.median_or_divider lies.

scenarios.name: blind

scenarios.name: occasion_b
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupies divided highway h during the first part of its left turn's window; the turn carries it across h's divider, where it has no opening, into a driveway beyond h: the trigger held for part of the turn and no opening or intersection was overlapped.

scenarios.name: occasion_b_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject left divided highway h before its turn window began and makes a U-turn on an undivided highway: the trigger held only before the turn.

scenarios.name: occasion_f
scenarios.narrative: The subject's U-turn on h overlaps a divider region carrying the opening attribute during part of its window.

scenarios.name: occasion_f_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject overlapped a divider opening on h only before its turn window began; the U-turn itself crosses the divider where it has no opening and overlaps no intersection.

scenarios.name: occasion_g
scenarios.narrative: The subject's left turn on h overlaps an intersection lying on h during part of its window.

scenarios.name: occasion_g_outside
scenarios.narrative: The subject occupied an intersection on h only before its turn window began; it then makes a U-turn across the divider mid-block, overlapping no opening and no intersection.

under_way.words: its heading change over the window behind the observation
under_way.justification: The turn is under way within the window behind its recognition, over which prim.heading_change integrates kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading'): the road user's motion, not the region it occupies, tells the turn from what came before.

segmentation.text: When a vehicle
enters an intersection
controlled by a traffic-control signal which is installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered,
but is inoperative at the time the vehicle enters the intersection,
the driver of the vehicle

shall proceed as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance to the intersection and shall stop at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After making such a stop,
the driver shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles which have previously completed a stop
or are within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate: the atom's literal argument is an aggregate id'.

The entry is the observation at which the subject's footprint comes to overlap the intersection X (rel.occupies; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet'), having at the previous observation occupied a carrier c that enters X: st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.travel_region is the kind of c. The carrier is the source's record, never read from distance or velocity.

dev.traffic_signal: 'a signal head; ... uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered' — 'installed and has its vehicular signals uncovered'. 'Controlled by' is dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection, read as control of the junction itself': the signal governs c or X. Not a stand-in for a position: governance, not the head's location, decides.

dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication' — exactly 'installed ... uncovered, but is inoperative'; read at the entry observation, 'at the time the vehicle enters the intersection'.

'The driver of the vehicle' is the vehicle's controlled motion (DEF-NRS-484A-080 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle'), read through the vehicle of the admitted aggregate.

Proceeding 'as if a stop sign had been erected at each entrance' requires, at the subject's own entrance (its carrier c with st.lane_enters c X), the stop a stop sign requires before entering X (rel.occupies); the stop is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement' (the definition whose scope is a stop 'when required'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 concerns stopping when prohibited), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt. Its place, in the words' order: st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') tied to c by st.entrance_of ('the carrier whose entrance into an intersection a stop line or a crosswalk marks'), its side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction) given by prim.region_offset_along and the body-to-line distance by st.region_geometry; else st.crosswalk ('marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection') marking c's entrance, 'before entering' being a footprint not overlapping it; else c's entrance end, the footprint not overlapping X and the body within the stop-point tolerance of it. Distance never stands for the association, which st.entrance_of records. 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'): the view of its approaching members is a perception read through the place it describes.

applicability: At the subject's entry into an intersection X: the observation at which its footprint overlaps X and did not at the previous observation, where at that previous observation it occupied a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X); and where at the entry observation a traffic signal d governs c or X (dev.governs) and d is inoperative (dev.inoperative).
obligation: Search for the stop: the subject made a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt with speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance) while occupying c at the place for c, in the words' order: (1) where a stop line marks c's entrance (st.entrance_of(line, c)), a halt with the line ahead of or at the subject's reference point along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along at or above zero) and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the line (st.region_geometry distance); (2) where no stop line marks c (every line's entrance list is observed and excludes c), a halt with the footprint not overlapping the crosswalk marking c's entrance, that crosswalk ahead along c's direction (prim.region_offset_along above zero) and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (3) where neither marks c, a halt with the footprint not overlapping X and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start — the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it along c's direction, and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance; where several marks of that kind mark c, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into X, whichever comes later. A halt found: compliant; either end reached without one: violated; neither end reached (the recording begins with the subject inside the zone): unknown. Each entry owes its own halt; only an observed exit from the zone upstream begins a new approach. The entry is unknown where the previous observation does not show the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown. No bound is taken from the recording's start, a first observation or a cumulative distance.

narrowings.why: 'clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is read as c's entrance end into X, the point nearest the intersection outside it: the view is a perception read through the place the words describe, and no sight distance is measured. At an intersection with an inoperative signal the 'through highway' is each other way meeting there.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.traffic_signal governs carrier c, which enters X; at the subject's entry into X it is dev.inoperative. A st.stop_line marks c's entrance; the subject crosses it and enters X at a kin.speed well above p.halt_speed_tolerance, never halting since it was upstream of the line's stopping zone.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject halts (kin.speed at or below p.halt_speed_tolerance) on c with the stop line just ahead within p.stop_point_tolerance, then enters X.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing c shows circular_green at the subject's entry into X: not inoperative.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A traffic signal governs c; dev.inoperative is absent on the source, so whether the signal is inoperative at the entry is unknown.

scenarios.name: history_boundary
scenarios.narrative: Inoperative signal governing c; the recording begins with the subject already within p.stop_point_tolerance of the stop line, moving slowly; no halt is recorded before it enters X.
scenarios.boundary: the approach start: the subject's last observation outside the stop line's stopping zone upstream on c lies before the recording

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: No stop line and no crosswalk mark c (entrance lists observed, excluding c); the subject halts with its footprint outside X and its body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X, then enters.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A stop line marks c; the subject passes it without halting and halts only at the crosswalk beyond it, then enters X: the halt is not at the governing place.

param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin

dev.traffic_signal: 'a signal head; ... uncovered attribute for an installed head whose faces are not covered'; 'controlled by' is dev.governs ('the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection') on c or X.
dev.inoperative: 'a signal head installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication', read at the subject's entry observation, 'at the time the vehicle enters'.
'The driver of the vehicle' is the vehicle's controlled motion, read through the vehicle of the admitted aggregate.

'yielding' maps as in the index: the subject does not proceed in preference to the other vehicle — its kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') stays at or below the halt tolerance while the other is in conflict — and does not collide with it (rel.contact, 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'). kin.speed is not a stand-in for acceleration; contact is not a near miss, which the standard bounds.

'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate. 'Previously completed a stop' is another vehicle v's complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, DEF-NRS-484A-255 'complete cessation from movement') while occupying its own approach carrier c2 of X (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) before entering X, its halt beginning before the subject's own halt on c: the order of stops at an intersection where every entrance is treated as stop-controlled.
'are within the intersection': v's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet').

operationalizations.standard: proceed cautiously: proceed without creating a danger of a crash with the vehicles the words name
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the subject proceeds (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while, under constant velocities, its centre and the other vehicle's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance — a present danger of a crash

applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and has overlapped it continuously since its latest entry into X (the observation at which it came to overlap X, having occupied at the observation before a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X)), where at that entry observation a traffic signal governing c or X (dev.governs) was inoperative (dev.inoperative), and where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 (binder subject ↦ subject) was complied with at that entry observation: 'After making such a stop' — the stop that rule searches for, read at the entry by a past operator.
obligation: Re-binding X and c as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that either (a) occupies X, or (b) occupies a carrier c2 entering X (st.lane_enters c2 X), on which, without overlapping X, it came to a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, p.halt_speed_tolerance) whose onset lies earlier than the onset of the subject's last halt on c before its entry (or the subject made none), having occupied c2 or X at every observation since: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'cautiously' is read only through the yielding the words join to it: proceeding without a present danger of a crash with the vehicles named; no further speed bound is read.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject halted at the stop line of c (inoperative dev.traffic_signal governing c) and entered X; vehicle v occupies X crossing from the subject's right; the subject moves on with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject stays at rest just inside X until v has cleared, then proceeds with no closest approach to v below p.conflict_centre_clearance within p.conflict_horizon.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The signal governing c showed circular_green at the subject's entry: not inoperative.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: After its stop the subject is in X with v crossing on a conflicting path; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: After its stop the subject crosses X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Vehicle v halted on its own approach after the subject's halt and still waits there; the subject crosses X and its closest approach to v is predicted below p.conflict_centre_clearance: v is not a vehicle that previously completed a stop and is not within X.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject entered X without halting at the stop line (NRS_484B_250_4_o1 violated at its entry), then crosses X in conflict with v: the yielding duty follows 'such a stop', which was not made; the omitted stop is judged by NRS_484B_250_4_o1.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
approaching an intersection
shall yield
the right-of-way
to a vehicle which has entered the intersection
from a different highway.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion, not membership.

Same mapping as 'approaching the intersection' in the index: the subject occupies (rel.occupies) a carrier c1 whose entrance end is X — st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end — the carrier is an approach to that intersection'; st.travel_region is c1's kind, st.intersection X's. Never read from distance or velocity.

Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed — kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') above the halt tolerance — while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact 'the bodies of two road users ... touch or overlap (a collision)'). Contact is not a near miss; the near miss is the standard's bound.

'A vehicle' is the admitted aggregate; 'which has entered the intersection' is its footprint overlapping X (rel.occupies), continuously since the observation at which it came from its approach carrier (f).

'From a different highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way') is v's approach carrier c2 (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c2 X) lying on a highway h2 (st.on_way: 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') on which the subject's carrier c1 does not lie. st.on_way is not nearness to a way: the relation is the map's.

Same mapping as 'or at a traffic-controlled intersection' in the index. DEF-NRS-484A-145: 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic'; the intersection is controlled where a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering it (dev.governs: 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls ... or an intersection'; st.lane_enters ties the carrier to X).

'Vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions': per rel.oncoming's 'Not a stand-in for: the direction a road user approaches from — that is read through the carrier it approaches through ... and through that carrier's direction (st.lane_direction)'. The subject's carrier c1 and the carrier c2 v entered X from (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) have designated directions opposed within p.oncoming_heading_cos. 'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate.

'Is making a left turn' is the turn under way in X: the vehicle's heading change since its entry into X (rel.occupies), integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left') by the formula language's heading-since term, lying to the left between p.turn_heading_min and p.u_turn_heading_min. kin.yaw_rate is not a stand-in for road curvature: it is the vehicle's own turning.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a carrier c1 that enters an intersection X (st.lane_enters c1 X): the subject approaching X; except where X is controlled — a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X (dev.governs) — and except where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 (binder subject ↦ subject) applies to the subject.
obligation: Re-binding c1 and X as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle whose footprint overlaps X and has overlapped it continuously since an observation at which v occupied a carrier c2 that enters X (st.lane_enters c2 X) and lies on a highway h2 (st.on_way c2 h2) on which c1 does not lie — excepting the pair where the designated directions of c1 and c2 (st.lane_direction) have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos and either the subject or v declares int.left_turn at X at this observation, or v's heading change since its latest entry into X (heading-since over kin.yaw_rate, step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is a turn to the left of at least p.turn_heading_min and below p.u_turn_heading_min: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'official' is a legal status; the device present and governing is its evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: No device governs X or its carriers. Vehicle v entered X from carrier c2 on highway h2, on which the subject's carrier c1 does not lie, and is crossing X. The subject on c1 keeps kin.speed well above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject comes to rest on c1 short of X until v has cleared, then proceeds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.stop_sign governs c1: the intersection is controlled.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X; v crossing X from a different highway on a conflicting path; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject approaches the uncontrolled X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v is approaching X on its own carrier and has not entered X; the subject's closest approach to v is in conflict, but v is not a vehicle which has entered the intersection.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: At a skewed junction v entered X from c2 on another highway whose designated direction is opposed to c1's within p.oncoming_heading_cos, and v declares int.left_turn at X; the subject proceeds in conflict with v: the pair is excepted.

segmentation.text: When two vehicles
enter an intersection
from different highways
at approximately the same time,
the driver of the vehicle on the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle on the right.
Except as otherwise provided in subsection 4 [NRS-484B-250-4],
this section does not apply at intersections controlled by official traffic-control devices
or to vehicles approaching each other from opposite directions,
when the driver of one of the vehicles is intending to
or is making a left turn.

elements.justification: 'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'): the subject and the other vehicle v both.

Two vehicles 'enter' at approximately the same time when they reach its entrance together: a vehicle that yields at the edge never enters together with the other, so the entering the words time is each vehicle's arrival at X — occupying a carrier entering X (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), its body comes within the stop-point tolerance of X, the bound within which a vehicle is at a mark (st.region_geometry, 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it (zero when they overlap)'). Not a stand-in for occupancy: the distance reads arrival at the edge, the carrier fixes which intersection.

'From different highways' (DEF-NRS-484A-095): the two approach carriers c1, c2 (st.lane_enters) lie on ways (st.on_way, 'the public way (a highway region) a structure region lies on') such that c2 lies on a highway on which c1 does not lie.
The subject is the vehicle on the left: the other vehicle lies on its right, rel.bearing 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" ...)'. 'Driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while v is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).
'The vehicle on the right': v of the admitted aggregate whose bearing in the subject's frame (rel.bearing) has a negative lateral component (to the right) at the later of the two arrivals.

Same mapping as 'or at a traffic-controlled intersection' in the index: a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X (dev.governs; DEF-NRS-484A-145 'every sign, signal, marking and device ... for the purpose of regulating, warning or guiding traffic').

Per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, the direction a road user approaches from is read through its approach carrier and that carrier's st.lane_direction: c1 and c2 have designated directions opposed within p.oncoming_heading_cos.

'Is making a left turn': the vehicle's heading change since its entry into X (rel.occupies), integrated from kin.yaw_rate ('positive when the heading turns to the left'), lies to the left between p.turn_heading_min and p.u_turn_heading_min.

operationalizations.standard: approximately the same time: the two arrivals at the intersection's edge are close enough in time that neither vehicle can clear before the other arrives
operationalizations.convention: arrival of each vehicle is the observation (kin.time) at which its body first comes within p.stop_point_tolerance of X on a carrier entering X; the two arrivals are at approximately the same time where their times differ by no more than p.same_time_arrival_window, a two-second headway

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

applicability: At every observation at which the subject has arrived at an intersection X — its arrival: the latest observation at which, occupying a carrier c1 with st.lane_enters(c1, X), its body came within p.stop_point_tolerance of X (st.region_geometry distance) having not been within it at the observation before — and has occupied c1 or X at every observation since; except where X is controlled (a traffic signal, stop sign or yield sign governs X or a carrier entering X), and except where NRS_484B_250_4_o1 or NRS_484B_250_4_o2 (binder subject ↦ subject) applies to the subject.
obligation: Re-binding c1 and X as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle that arrived at X in the same way on a carrier c2 entering X, c2 lying on a highway (st.on_way) on which c1 does not lie, with the two arrivals no more than p.same_time_arrival_window apart (time since each arrival), v lying on the subject's right at the later of the two arrivals (rel.bearing lateral component negative), and v occupying c2 or X at every observation since its arrival — excepting the pair where c1's and c2's designated directions have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos and the subject or v declares int.left_turn at X at this observation or v's heading change since its latest entry into X (heading-since over kin.yaw_rate, step p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph) is a left turn of at least p.turn_heading_min and below p.u_turn_heading_min: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'official' is a legal status; the device present and governing is its evidence.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X. The subject on c1 and v on c2 (on another highway) arrive within p.same_time_arrival_window of each other; v lies to the subject's right (rel.bearing). The subject proceeds with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance and its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same arrivals; the subject comes to rest at X's edge until v has crossed, then proceeds.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A dev.yield_sign governs c1: X is controlled.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Uncontrolled X; simultaneous arrivals from different highways; the subject proceeds in conflict with v; rel.bearing is absent, so which vehicle is on the right is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: Simultaneous arrivals; v lies to the subject's left; the subject proceeds first in conflict with v: no vehicle on its right is owed the right-of-way.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v on the subject's right arrives several times p.same_time_arrival_window after the subject; the subject proceeds: not approximately the same time.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: The subject arrives at uncontrolled X with no other road user in the scene.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Within an intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... intersection ...)'; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet').
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).

'Any vehicle' is the admitted aggregate. 'Approaching from the opposite direction', per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, is read through the carrier v approaches through (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters c2 X) and its st.lane_direction, opposed to the direction of the carrier c1 the subject entered X from, within p.oncoming_heading_cos — never from current headings, which the subject's turn changes.
'Which is within the intersection': v's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies), having come from c2.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

operationalizations.standard: so close to the intersection as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a vehicle approaching on its carrier is an immediate hazard where, under constant velocities, its centre and the subject's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance

applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and the subject declares int.left_turn at X (intent subject X) at that observation.
obligation: Re-binding X as in the applicability, and c1 as the carrier entering X (st.lane_enters c1 X) the subject occupied when it last entered X (it has overlapped X continuously since an observation at which it occupied c1): for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle approaching from the opposite direction — v occupies a carrier c2 entering X, or overlaps X continuously since an observation at which it occupied such a c2, where the designated directions of c1 and c2 (st.lane_direction) have a dot product below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos — and that either overlaps X or, on c2, has its closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: The subject overlaps X and declares int.left_turn at X; v approaches on c2, whose st.lane_direction is opposed to that of the subject's entry carrier c1; the subject moves into its turn with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance while its closest approach to v lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject stays at rest in X until v has passed, then turns.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: The subject crosses X with int.left_turn declared false at X (its plan goes straight).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Left-turning subject in X, opposing v in conflict; kin.speed is absent, so whether the subject proceeds into the conflict is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject turns left in X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: v approaches from a cross street (its carrier's direction perpendicular to c1's) on a conflicting path; the subject turns: v does not approach from the opposite direction.

segmentation.text: The driver of a vehicle
within an intersection
intending to turn to the left
shall yield
the right-of-way
to any vehicle approaching from the opposite direction
which is within the intersection
or so close thereto as to constitute an immediate hazard,
but such driver, having so yielded
and having given a signal when and as required,
may make such left turn
and the drivers of all other vehicles
approaching the intersection from the opposite direction
shall yield
the right-of-way
to the vehicle making the left turn.

elements.justification: The turning vehicle t: 'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle (ru.aggregate 'membership of a legal aggregate'); its driver is its controlled motion.
t 'within an intersection': t's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies; st.intersection 'the region where two roadways meet').

'Having given a signal when and as required' of a left turn: sig.turn_indicator 'state ∈ {off, left, right}' at left, or sig.hand_signal 'meaning ∈ {..., left, ...}' at left — the two manners a signal of turning is given — at some observation since t came onto the carrier c1 it entered X from: the signal is required on the approach to the turn and through it, which is when the words look for it. The indicator is not a stand-in for the turn itself, which k reads separately.
'May make such left turn': t is making its turn, moving (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) within X (rel.occupies) since its current movement within X began, with its left-turn plan declared (c).
'The drivers of all other vehicles': the subject, of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, other than t; 'drivers' read through the vehicles' controlled motion.

'Approaching the intersection': the subject occupies a carrier c2 whose entrance end is X (st.lane_enters, 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end') and does not yet overlap X; 'from the opposite direction', per rel.oncoming's not-a-stand-in clause, is c2's st.lane_direction opposed to that of the carrier c1 t entered X from, within p.oncoming_heading_cos.
Same mapping as 'shall yield' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while t is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).
'The vehicle making the left turn' is t, of the admitted aggregate, within X (rel.occupies) making the turn the conditions a, b, c, i, j, k describe.

operationalizations.standard: the right-of-way: precedence owed where 'circumstances of direction, speed and proximity ... give rise to the danger of a crash' (DEF-NRS-484A-210)
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: a danger of a crash exists where, under constant velocities, the two centres approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance; the subject proceeds where its speed exceeds p.halt_speed_tolerance

applicability: At every observation at which the subject occupies a carrier c2 that enters an intersection X (st.lane_enters c2 X) and does not overlap X, and some other road user t of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle: overlaps X; declares int.left_turn at X at this observation; entered X (overlapping it continuously since) from a carrier c1 entering X whose designated direction has a dot product with c2's below minus p.oncoming_heading_cos; has been moving within X (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) at every observation since its current movement began — the later of its latest entry into X and its latest rise above p.halt_speed_tolerance while in X; showed a left signal (sig.turn_indicator left or sig.hand_signal left) at some observation since it came onto c1; and complied with NRS_484B_253_o1 (binder subject ↦ t) at the observation at which that current movement began: 'having so yielded'.
obligation: Re-binding X and c2, and quantifying every road user t as in the applicability: for every such t, the subject is not in contact with t (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, t; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, t; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'the drivers' are read through the vehicles' controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls them.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
When proper signs have been erected,
the driver of a vehicle

shall stop or yield at a clearly marked stop line or, if there is none, before entering the crosswalk on the near side of the intersection or, if there is none, then at the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway.
After having stopped or, in the event of a yield sign, slowed or stopped,
the driver shall yield
the right-of-way
to other vehicles which have entered the intersection from such through highway
or which are approaching so closely on such through highway as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic ('pedestrians, ridden or herded animals, vehicles and other conveyances ... using any highway'), of which the subject is a member. 'Being controlled by a police officer' (DEF-NRS-484A-180 'every officer authorized to direct or regulate traffic') is dev.human_direction, 'a person directing traffic ... role ∈ {police_officer, ...}', of role police_officer governing (dev.governs) the subject's carrier c or X (st.travel_region), read at the subject's entry.

'Being controlled by ... a traffic-control signal' (DEF-NRS-484A-290 'by which traffic is alternately directed to stop or proceed'): a dev.traffic_signal governing c or X (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'): a dark signal directs nothing.

'Proper signs' are a dev.stop_sign ('regulatory sign requiring a full halt') or dev.yield_sign ('regulatory sign requiring yielding without a mandatory halt') governing (dev.governs) the carrier c the subject occupies (rel.occupies) whose entrance end is X (st.lane_enters), or X itself. Governance, not the sign's position, ties it to the approach.
Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Stop' is DEF-NRS-484A-255, 'complete cessation from movement' (the definition whose scope is a stop 'when required'; DEF-NRS-484A-260 applies when stopping is prohibited), carried by drv.motion.complete_halt; at a stop sign it is owed. 'Yield' at a yield sign is, in the words of the next sentence, 'slowed or stopped': the subject's kin.speed ('magnitude of velocity') within the place's stopping zone is at or below the speed from which it still halts at the place (p.yield_line_speed_max), a halt included. The place, in the words' order: st.stop_line ('the transverse line marking where vehicles halt for a device') tied to c by st.entrance_of, its side along c's designated direction (st.lane_direction) given by prim.region_offset_along, the body-to-line distance by st.region_geometry; else st.crosswalk marking c's entrance, 'before entering' being a footprint not overlapping it (rel.occupies); else c's entrance end into X (st.intersection), the footprint outside X. Distance never stands for the association. 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic; the view of its approaching members is a perception read through the place the words describe.

applicability: At the subject's entry into an intersection X: the observation at which its footprint overlaps X and did not at the previous observation, where at that previous observation it occupied a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X); where at the entry observation a stop sign or a yield sign governs c or X (dev.governs); except where at that observation a police officer's direction (dev.human_direction of role police_officer) governs c or X, or a traffic signal that is not inoperative (dev.inoperative false) governs c or X.
obligation: Search for the act on the approach: where a stop sign governs c or X, a complete halt (drv.motion.complete_halt, speed_tol p.halt_speed_tolerance); where only a yield sign does, an observation at which the subject's kin.speed is at or below p.yield_line_speed_max (a halt included) — in either case while occupying c within the stopping zone of the place for c, in the words' order: (1) where a stop line marks c's entrance (st.entrance_of(line, c)), the line ahead of or at the subject's reference point along c's designated direction (prim.region_offset_along at or above zero) and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of the line (st.region_geometry distance); (2) where no stop line marks c (every line's entrance list observed and excluding c), the footprint not overlapping the crosswalk marking c's entrance, that crosswalk ahead along c's direction and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of it; (3) where neither marks c, the footprint not overlapping X and the body within p.stop_point_tolerance of X. History bound: the search runs back from the entry and ends at the approach start — the last observation before the entry at which the subject, on a carrier the place marks, is outside the place's stopping zone upstream (off the mark, short of it along c's direction and farther from it than p.stop_point_tolerance; where several marks of that kind mark c, outside and short of each) — or at the subject's previous entry into X, whichever is later. Act found: compliant; either end reached without it: violated; neither end reached (the recording begins inside the zone): unknown. Each entry owes its own act; only an observed exit from the zone upstream begins a new approach. The entry is unknown where the previous observation does not show the subject on a mapped carrier; where a mark's association with c is unobserved and the verdict turns on it, unknown. No bound is taken from the recording's start, a first observation or a cumulative distance.

narrowings.why: 'proper signs have been erected' is a legal status; a stop or yield sign present and governing the approach is its evidence.
'clearly marked' is read as the stop line the scene represents; the paint's clarity is not modelled.

'the point nearest the intersection where the driver has a view of approaching traffic on the through highway' is read as c's entrance end into X, the point nearest the intersection outside it: the view is a perception read through the place the words describe; no sight distance is measured.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign,
in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1],
prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway
and shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield
and which are within the intersection
or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

scenarios.narrative: A stop sign governs c, but an operating dev.traffic_signal (circular_red) also governs c at the subject's entry.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.stop_point_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the body-to-mark gap within which a halt counts as at the mark: a stop line's set-back before a crossing plus a placement margin
param_proposals.source: MUTCD stop line placement in advance of a crosswalk

param_proposals.name: p.yield_line_speed_max
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a vehicle at the place of a yield sign counts as having slowed: the speed from which a passenger car can still halt within the stop-point tolerance at a comfortable deceleration of about 4.5 m/s^2
param_proposals.source: AASHTO comfortable deceleration rate of the stopping sight distance model

segmentation.text: Except when traffic is being controlled by a police officer
or a traffic-control signal:
The driver of a vehicle
shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or yield in compliance with a yield sign,
in compliance with the manner prescribed in subsection 1 [NRS-484B-257-1],
prior to entering an intersection
if a stop sign or a yield sign is erected at one or more entrances thereto
although not a part of a through highway
and shall proceed cautiously,
yielding
to vehicles not so obligated to stop or yield
and which are within the intersection
or approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
during the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection.

elements.justification: 'Traffic' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic, of which the subject is a member; 'being controlled by a police officer' is dev.human_direction of role police_officer governing (dev.governs) the subject's approach carrier c or X (st.travel_region), read at the subject's entry.
A dev.traffic_signal governing c or X (dev.governs) that is not dev.inoperative ('installed and uncovered but showing no valid indication'), read at the subject's entry.
Same mapping as 'The driver of a vehicle' in the index: the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle; 'driver' is the vehicle's controlled motion.

'Such driver' is the one so obliged: a dev.stop_sign or dev.yield_sign governs (dev.governs) the carrier c (st.lane_enters c X) the subject occupied (rel.occupies) when it entered X, or X itself — one of the 'one or more entrances' the words name.
Same mapping as 'yielding' in the index: the subject does not proceed (kin.speed above the halt tolerance) while the protected vehicle is in conflict, and does not collide with it (rel.contact).

'Vehicles' is the admitted aggregate. 'Not so obligated to stop or yield' is v whose approach carrier c2 of X (rel.occupies, st.lane_enters) is governed (dev.governs) by no stop sign and no yield sign, nor is X.
'Which are within the intersection': v's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies), continuously since it occupied c2.
'During the time such driver is moving across or within the intersection': the subject's footprint overlaps X (rel.occupies) and its kin.speed is above the halt tolerance.

operationalizations.standard: proceed cautiously: proceed without creating a danger of a crash with the vehicles the words name
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: the subject proceeds (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while, under constant velocities, its centre and the other vehicle's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance — a present danger of a crash

operationalizations.standard: approaching so closely as to constitute an immediate hazard
operationalizations.convention: traffic-conflict technique: v approaching on its carrier is an immediate hazard where, under constant velocities, its centre and the subject's approach within the time-to-collision threshold p.conflict_horizon to a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance

residues.why: 'although' is concessive: the duty reaches signed entrances whether or not the intersection is part of a through highway, and the yielding owed by a driver entering through a signed entrance is the same in both cases; the words withhold the duty nowhere.

applicability: At every observation at which the subject's footprint overlaps an intersection X and has overlapped it continuously since its latest entry into X (having occupied at the observation before a carrier c with st.lane_enters(c, X)) and the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance); where at that entry observation a stop sign or a yield sign governed c or X (dev.governs), no police officer's direction (dev.human_direction of role police_officer) governed c or X, and no traffic signal that was not inoperative governed c or X.
obligation: Re-binding X and c as in the applicability: for every other road user v of DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle not so obligated — v occupies a carrier c2 entering X, or overlaps X continuously since an observation at which it occupied such a c2, where no stop sign and no yield sign governs c2 or X (dev.governs) — and that either overlaps X or, on c2, has its closest approach to the subject within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance: the subject is not in contact with v (rel.contact), and it is not the case that the subject is moving (kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance) while prim.closest_approach_within(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) holds with prim.closest_approach_distance(subject, v; p.conflict_horizon) below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

narrowings.why: 'cautiously' is read only through the yielding the words join to it: proceeding without a present danger of a crash with the vehicles named; no further speed bound is read.
'the driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A dev.yield_sign governs c; the subject entered X and moves across it with kin.speed above p.halt_speed_tolerance; v occupies X having entered from c2, which no stop or yield sign governs; their closest approach lies within p.conflict_horizon at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: Same scene; the subject waits at rest until v has cleared, then moves across X with no closest approach to v within the bound.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: No stop or yield sign governs c or X when the subject enters X.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: Subject moving across X in conflict with v; dev.governs is absent, so whether a sign governs c, and whether v is so obligated, are unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: The subject moves across X with no other road user in the scene.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: At an all-way stop, v entered X from c2, which a stop sign governs; the subject moves in conflict with v: v is itself obligated to stop, and this duty does not protect it.

param_proposals.name: p.halt_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: the speed at or below which a sampled speed counts as no movement: the source's speed resolution
param_proposals.source: speed resolution of the acquisition standard's kinematic channels

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_horizon
param_proposals.convention: time-to-collision threshold of the traffic-conflict technique: a closest approach later than this is not a present danger of a crash
param_proposals.source: traffic conflict technique time-to-collision thresholds

param_proposals.name: p.conflict_centre_clearance
param_proposals.convention: centre-to-centre distance at the closest approach below which the bodies of a passenger car and another road user are taken to collide or nearly collide: about a car's half-length plus half a body width
param_proposals.source: design passenger-car dimensions
